title: The Agriculture Building
about: A yearly tradition of visiting the Swenson Vineyards display in the Agriculture Building, a piece of family history connected to my great-grandfather. Each year I'd find the display, take a picture, and send it to my grandma. This year, I discovered that almost all of it had disappeared, leaving only a photograph behind.
description:
This track tells the story of a small tradition I had whenever I visited the fair: finding the Swenson Vineyards display in the Agriculture Building. The vineyards belonged to my great-grandfather, so the exhibit was more than something to look at. It was a visible piece of my family's history. Each year I'd stop, take a picture, and send it to my grandma.

This year was different. What had once been an entire display had been reduced to a single photograph. I still stopped, took my picture, and sent it to Grandma, only now the tradition carried a different meaning. The song reflects on watching a piece of family history slowly disappear from a public place while knowing that the history, the connection, and the reason I stop there remain even as the exhibit itself fades away.
lyrics: There used to be a whole display,
A little piece of where we came from
Every year I'd stop to see it,
Every year I'd take the time.
No matter what else filled the day.
I'd stop and take a picture,
A little piece of family history
But this year when I went looking,
What once had filled an exhibit
Where our history once was found.
Can disappear a piece at a time.
Like I had every other day.
But I took that picture too,
And sent what still remained there
Home to Grandma like I do.
Won't be hanging on the wall.
Maybe no one walking past it
Will know the name at all.
But I know why I stop there,
It's more than just an exhibit—
It's where our family comes through.
Gets a little smaller every day.
As long as something's left there,
To bring back home to you.
